newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waterford seeks Rosenthal profit in 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Waterford seeks Rosenthal profit in 3 yrs.

text.p: Waterford Wedgwood plans to return ailing German porcelain firm Rosenthal AG to profit in the next three years but can only do so if it has an adequate stake, Waterford's financial director told Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung in an interview published on Thursday.

Richard Barnes said Waterford could eventually increase its stake in Rosenthal to between 47 percent and 49 percent but added that the size of the stake depended on Rosenthal's economic performance, the newspaper said.
"There is no firm target," Barnes was quoted as saying.

Waterford Wedgwood announced in December it planned to purchase an initial 9.1 percent shareholding through the issue by Rosenthal of 60,000 shares. Rosenthal shareholders vote on the move at an extraordinary general meeting on Friday, January 31.
Waterford Wedgwood also has an option to buy a further 15 percent of Rosenthal over the next four years.
The newspaper said Barnes "indicated" that Rosenthal would conduct a further capital raising this year in which Waterford Wedgwood might participate. The newspaper did not directly quote him.

Barnes said Rosenthal was an "excellent brand" which gave it a market share of 25 percent in Germany. He said Waterford Wedgwood's traditional and classical styles of chinaware complemented Rosenthal's more modern products.
He said Rosenthal's weakness was high production costs which explained why its exports were weak.

Asked how Waterford Wedgwood planned to cut production costs at Rosenthal, Barnes said it was too early to say but noted that a relatively high percentage of Rosenthal's production was based in Germany.
